Second batch of the #500 privacy scrub — a one-time backfill; the write-path redaction feature keeps new records clean:

- \`jdoe\` → \`user\` in doc examples (\`docs/agent-teams.md\`, \`docs/build-plan-des011.md\`) and the redaction tests' own fixtures (\`internal/hook/audit_content_test.go\`, \`audit_entry_test.go\`, \`internal/mission/redact_test.go\`)

- Home paths and emails in one mission result and two committed session audit chunks replaced with \`[REDACTED:home-path]\` / \`[REDACTED:email]\`

## Why the diff includes a quarantine

The original hand-scrub used a raw line-regex tool that corrupted JSON — email matches consumed escape prefixes (\`\\n\\n@pytest…\` → invalid \`\\[\`), secret-shaped matches truncated lines mid-object. The audit-seal pre-commit hook **correctly refused the corrupt chunks (fail-closed working as designed)**. This PR:

2. Quarantines one same-cause corrupt chunk from the current session via \`ethos audit quarantine\` (the sanctioned path): fully recovered into a fresh chunk; the retired \`.corrupt\` file and \`.quarantine\` marker travel as evidence

## Deliberate non-change

\`tool_input_hash\` values in scrubbed chunks are unchanged — they attest the original pre-redaction inputs; recomputing them would forge history.

## Verification

- \`make check\` green pre- and post-rebase (full suite incl. \`go test -race\`, validate-content)
- Whole-tree JSONL validation scan: 0 invalid lines remaining
- Pre-commit seal passes (it was the failing gate that caught the corruption)

import json, pathlib
files = [
  ".punt-labs/ethos/sessions/2026-05-23-f8f75233-e179-460c-8871-f243bc3b1a85/audit.jsonl",
  ".punt-labs/ethos/sessions/2026-08-20-94901c4f-5d86-41c5-bd06-98cbd86216b8/audit-1787125083841877647-1787178320813044578.jsonl",
]
import os
os.chdir("<repo>")
for f in files:
    p = pathlib.Path(f)
    out, marked = [], 0
    for line in p.read_text().splitlines():
        if "[REDACTED:" in line:
            obj = json.loads(line)
            if not obj.get("redacted"):
                obj["redacted"] = True
                marked += 1
            line = json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
            json.loads(line)  # revalidate
        out.append(line)
    p.write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n")
    print(f"{f}: marked {marked} lines redacted=true, all revalidated")
EOF
